what_its_for: Plecanatide is used to treat adults who have chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) or irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C). These are conditions where you have ongoing constipation that is not caused by another medical problem. This medicine helps your bowels move more regularly and makes stools easier to pass.
how_to_take: Take plecanatide by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with water. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, you can crush the tablet and mix it with a teaspoon of room-temperature applesauce or water, then swallow the mixture right away. Do not save the mixture for later. You can also mix the crushed tablet in a small amount of water and give it through a nasogastric (NG) or gastric tube if needed — ask your doctor or pharmacist for specific instructions on this.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 3 mg (one tablet) taken once every day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not take more than the prescribed dose. This medicine is only approved for adults 18 years of age and older — it should NEVER be given to children under 6 years old, and it should be avoided in children ages 6 to 17 unless specifically directed by a doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Taking a double dose will not help you and may cause unwanted side effects.
storage: Store plecanatide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original bottle. Do not remove the desiccant (the small drying packet) from the bottle — this helps keep the tablets dry and effective. Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not give this medicine to children under 6 years of age, as it can cause serious harm or death due to severe diarrhea and dehydration. Store the medicine safely away from children. Avoid taking more than your prescribed dose. There are no specific foods or drinks you must avoid while taking plecanatide, but talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you develop severe diarrhea or diarrhea that does not stop, as this can lead to dangerous dehydration. Signs of dehydration include feeling dizzy or lightheaded, decreased urination, dry mouth, or feeling very thirsty. Also contact your doctor if your constipation does not improve, if you notice blood in your stool, if you have severe stomach pain or cramping, or if you have any new or worsening symptoms. Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements.
when_it_works: Some people may notice improvement in their bowel movements within the first week of starting plecanatide, but it may take a few weeks for the full benefit to be felt. Keep taking the medicine as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate results. If you do not feel any improvement after a few weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking plecanatide if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if plecanatide passes into breast milk. Children: This medicine is NOT approved for use in children under 18 years old. It must be kept away from young children because accidental ingestion can cause life-threatening diarrhea and dehydration. Older adults: No specific dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but always discuss your full health history with your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Plecanatide has not been well studied in people with severe kidney or liver problems — let your doctor know about any kidney or liver conditions you have.
